finding: Within its model, one image of ordinary ground holds almost nothing of the chamber, however it is read. The chamber reaches the image only through its echo, at least 347 dB down at X band (P2-11), or through the surface's motion during the pass; every method is a function of the image. For fully developed speckle, motion shared by the whole scene holds exactly none, and a rigorous bound on the finite change (the Fisher information with an explicit remainder) caps any test's detection rate above its false-alarm rate: 1.3e-09 under Giza's regional microseism level, 9.3e-08 at the noisiest stations on Earth, 1.3e-08 and 2.8e-08 at the measured 1-3 and 3-8 Hz levels (accuracy above a coin toss: half of each). With P2-26's dynamic imprint and the scattered wave counted unattenuated across the whole 5 km scene, the FTA's urban background for the whole pass gives 1.6e-03 (9.0e-03 over a room whose roof is 5 m down); a truck over a bump 15 m away for the whole pass, at its worst frequency (52 Hz) and the worst of four sampled sides, 2.3e-02 (1.2e-01). Those strong-shaking values are a restricted surrogate: the reference covariance is taken without the excitation's own motion, though the no-cavity world moves with it; P2-29's oracle with receiver noise, where motion common to both worlds cancels, bounds those cases validly. On a small image the exact likelihood-ratio test reaches 0.20 and 0.54 where Pinsker's bound from the exact KL allows 0.25 and 0.75 and weak-signal theory predicts 0.20 and 0.55: the ceiling sits 1.28 and 1.39 times above what the best test achieves, a bound, not an attained value. The model's Doppler-to-time relation (motion multiplied into the spectrum at each bin's stationary time) carries the same information as pulse-by-pulse physics to within 3.6% from 5 to 150 Hz on a 0.5 s aperture at the real chirp rate (at 0.5 Hz, a quarter cycle across it, the model holds 1.47 times more); with five cycles of motion across the aperture the model's excess falls from 6.1% to 0.07% as the time-bandwidth product rises from 1e+03 to 6e+04 (the real dwell's is 3e+06): an edge effect that fades, on the side of more information. The local extrapolation factor under the microseisms, 1e+09, is a scale within the model, not a physical shaking requirement.
